comment: The mutation set of the new path (SPEC 5.7, GG-0034; m3-plan G6): each mutant plants one realistic bug in the graalgo.go nodes/runtime, the scheduler, graalgo.syscall, the -toolexec emitter or the stdlib/ fork. 'old' must occur EXACTLY once in 'file' (check-repo verifies it per push). 'kill' names the per-push gate programs that must turn red (gate:program; gates: snapshot = a test/differential/corpus name, m1a/m1r/m1c/m1d/m1w13 = a program path of that gate); a mutant surviving them is re-run on every per-push differential gate in full. A survivor is either killed by a new program or carries a reviewed 'survivorJustification'. M1C-*/M1D-* were test/m1c and test/m1d's mutants.py lists.

mutants.description: SliceLoc.resolve (s[i] rvalue/lvalue) lets i == len(s) through: no 'index out of range [5] with length 5' panic; the element load runs past the slice (Java AIOOBE / backing-array garbage).
Slice-to-array(-pointer) conversion accepts a slice one element short of N (no 'cannot convert slice with length 3 to array or pointer to array with length 4').
Slice-of-slice s[lo:hi] / s[lo:hi:max] accepts hi == cap+1 (or max+1): no 'slice bounds out of range [:6] with capacity 5'; builds a slice with len > cap.
int32 wrap (NodeFactory.wrap for INT32 results and conversions) no longer truncates/sign-extends: int32 arithmetic and int32(x) conversions stop wrapping at 2^31.
When several select cases are ready the lowest-index one always wins (gc picks uniformly at random).
close(ch) dequeues plain receivers parked on ch and hands them (zero,false) but never unparks them: every goroutine blocked in <-ch / range ch at close time sleeps forever.
Every range over a map starts at entry 0: iteration order becomes deterministic insertion order (gc randomizes the start per range).

mutants.class: map iteration yields an entry twice
mutants.description: After wrapping around, the iterator stops one entry late: the entry at the random start index is produced twice per range (Go: each entry at most once).
Open-coded defers run FIFO (first deferred first) instead of LIFO.
recover() stops the panic from ANY function running while a deferred call unwinds, not only from the function called directly by the defer.
[]byte(s) shares the string's byte array when the string spans it exactly (no copy): writes through the slice mutate the immutable string.
mutants.old: return new Slice(new Flat(backing, Flat.NO_PRIMS, Flat.NO_REFS, s.toBytes()), 0, 0, 0, n, n);
mutants.new: return new Slice(new Flat(backing, Flat.NO_PRIMS, Flat.NO_REFS, s.off == 0 && s.b.length == n ? s.b : s.toBytes()), 0, 0, 0, n, n);

mutants.description: An invalid UTF-8 byte decodes as RuneError of width 2 (swallowing the next byte) instead of width 1, in range-over-string and []rune(s).
Cached interface == compares only the data words, not the dynamic types: any(1) == any(int64(1)) and two typed nil pointers of different types compare equal.
mutants.old: if (!(b instanceof Iface y) || y.type != cachedType) {

mutants.description: Comparing two interfaces holding the same uncomparable dynamic type returns false instead of panicking 'runtime error: comparing uncomparable type main.F'.
checkptr's misaligned-pointer fatal fires for pointer-free pointee types too (gc checks alignment only when the element type has pointers).
The timer heap becomes a max-heap: the latest deadline is waited for first and earlier timers fire late, in reverse order.
syscall.Exit/os.Exit collapse every non-zero code to 1.
An unrecovered panic (gc fatalpanic) exits with status 1 instead of 2; the report text is unchanged.
'fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!' exits with status 1 instead of 2.
the deadlock check ignores pending timers after main's runtime.Goexit: a program whose last goroutine sleeps on a timer dies with 'no goroutines (main called runtime.Goexit) - deadlock!'

A read/write deadline that expires while a goroutine waits in pollWait marks the descriptor timed out but never unparks the waiter: Read with SetReadDeadline hangs instead of returning os.ErrDeadlineExceeded.
mutants.survivorJustification: equivalent until m3-plan G7 (BUG-0060, measured 2026-11-25): no per-push program can reach this poller path — pipe fds block in the executor's blocking syscall instead of waiting for readiness in the poller, and every fd deadline expires at once (relative/absolute mix-up), so the mutated wake is never needed. Retire with BUG-0060's fix: the G7 lane adds a pipe-deadline program to test/m1d that kills it.

mutants.description: 3-clause for loops in go1.22+ files get pre-1.22 semantics: one shared loop variable captured by every closure.
mutants.old: if def, ok := st.Init.(*ir.DefineStmt); ok && fs.perIteration(s.Pos()) {

mutants.description: for k, v := range loops store every iteration into one shared variable instead of a fresh one (pre-Go 1.22 semantics): closures and pointers taken in the body all see the last value. (Replaces an emitter mutant of the GIR Range.PerIter flag, which the node package never reads: equivalent.)
mutants.old: return storeTo(target, r.define() ? r.fresh() : null, v, null);

mutants.description: Float constants are emitted in go/constant's short form (%.6g) instead of exactly: math.Pi becomes 3.14159, MaxFloat64 1.79769e+308.
Plain function calls are no longer hoisted ahead of the statement's plain operands (gc's order pass): operands are read strictly left to right around them.
uint64/uint/uintptr ordered comparisons are lowered to signed compares: values >= 2^63 compare as negative.
